The support FAQ, product guide, and customer interviews collectively describe scanned PDF handling as the most problematic ingestion case: scanned/image-only PDFs have no digital text layer, so KnowledgeHub’s standard parser extracts no text and cannot generate citations unless OCR is applied [NL-006-S03][NL-002-S08]. Without OCR, users get missing answers, no source citations, or citations pointing to the entire document rather than a specific page/paragraph [NL-021-S02][NL-024-S04]. The FAQ warns that OCR is heuristic and can misread blurry/low-resolution scans, handwriting, or complex layouts, causing broken citations, knowledge gaps, and longer processing times [NL-006-S03]. Recommended workarounds include exporting native text files like DOCX/Markdown instead of scans, excluding scans from the active corpus during pilots, converting tables to CSV/XLSX or using clear dark grid lines, and transcribing handwritten notes into digital text [NL-006-S03][NL-024-S04]. Customer interviews confirm the operational burden: teams must manually OCR thousands of legacy pages or delay uploads, and even then citation reliability suffers [NL-018-S05][NL-017-S06]. The planned solution was an Advanced OCR Pipeline targeted for August 2026 that would auto-detect image-only PDFs, extract text/layout, and enable page-specific citations [NL-006-S03][NL-024-S04][NL-018-S05][NL-017-S06]. The product guide additionally states PDFs have page/paragraph citation precision and enforces per-plan ingestion queue limits, while engineering discussions add that OCR batches need split queues, rate limits, page caps, and secure temporary storage [NL-002-S08][NL-021-S06].
